subject: general
question: Which of the following best explains the term 'formula unit mass'?

options.text: The mass of one mole of a substance
The mass of a single atom of an element
The mass of a single molecule of an element
The total mass of all atoms in one formula unit of a compound

solution:
The correct answer is __**The total mass of all atoms in one formula unit of a compound**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **formula unit mass** refers to the **total mass of all the atoms in one formula unit of a compound**. It is expressed in atomic mass units (amu).
 
• A **formula unit** represents the simplest ratio of ions in an ionic compound. For example, in NaCl, one formula unit consists of one sodium ion (Na⁺) and one chloride ion (Cl⁻).
 
• The **formula unit mass** is calculated by summing the atomic masses of all atoms present in the chemical formula of the compound. For instance, in NaCl, the formula unit mass = atomic mass of Na + atomic mass of Cl = 23 + 35.5 = 58.5 amu.
 
• The formula unit mass is particularly used for **ionic compounds** because these do not exist as discrete molecules but as a lattice structure. Hence, the term "formula unit" is used instead of "molecule."
 
• This concept is essential in stoichiometry, allowing chemists to calculate the mass relationships in chemical reactions involving ionic compounds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Atomic Mass:**

 
 
• The mass of an individual atom is expressed in atomic mass units (amu). For example, the atomic mass of sodium (Na) is approximately 23 amu, and that of chlorine (Cl) is 35.5 amu.
 
• The atomic mass is determined relative to the mass of one atom of carbon-12, which is defined as exactly 12 amu.
 
 
 
• **Formula Unit:**
 
 
• A formula unit is the smallest repeating unit of an ionic compound that represents its composition. For example, the formula unit of magnesium chloride is MgCl₂.
 
• It differs from a molecule because ionic compounds do not form discrete molecular entities but rather exist as a lattice of ions.
 
 
 
• **Difference Between Formula Unit Mass and Molecular Mass:**
 
 
• **Formula unit mass** is used for ionic compounds (e.g., NaCl, MgCl₂) and is based on the simplest ratio of ions.
 
• **Molecular mass** applies to covalent compounds (e.g., H₂O, CO₂) and is the sum of the atomic masses of all atoms in a molecule.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Formula Unit Mass:**
 
 
• It helps in calculating molar mass, which is crucial for stoichiometric calculations in chemistry.
 
• It is used to determine the proportions of elements in ionic compounds and their chemical behavior.
 
 
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• The formula unit mass of NaCl: 23 + 35.5 = 58.5 amu.
 
• The formula unit mass of MgCl₂: 24.3 + (2 × 35.5) = 95.3 amu.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Option 1:** "The mass of one mole of a substance" refers to molar mass, not formula unit mass. **This is incorrect.**
 
• **Option 2:** "The mass of a single atom of an element" refers to atomic mass, not formula unit mass. **This is incorrect.**
 
• **Option 3:** "The mass of a single molecule of an element" pertains to molecular mass, which is different from formula unit mass. **This is incorrect.**
 
• **Option 4:** "The total mass of all atoms in one formula unit of a compound" is the correct definition of formula unit mass. **This is correct.**
